div.div:
• edge/ — the only code that sees untrusted input: auth · CORS · rate limiting
• routes — /chat (SSE) · /verify · /conversations (+ pins) · /documents · /jobs; the last two are forwarded verbatim
• agent — 12 tools, a fast/deep/auto mode router, and a citation guard that matches every figure to a corpus reference
• sessions — durable conversation tree, compaction, interrupted-run recovery (own volume, ADR-0013)
• llm/ — the only place that calls Gemini
• the SSE vocabulary is frozen: update · token · complete · error

div.div:
• api — validate the upload, hash the bytes, write the blob, then ingest-submit (which answers 202)
• worker — claim a lease → run the pipeline → persist; at-least-once by design
• the pipeline does no catalog I/O — it returns a pure BuildResult, so it unit-tests with no DataHub at all
• persist replaces nodes, header, mentions and edges atomically — idempotent, safe to retry
• everything flows through DataHub's queue and stores: no database of its own

div.div:
• six capabilities, one package each; store.py yields the DataHub adapter for it
• hybrid retrieval — vector (halfvec cosine) and lexical (ts_rank_cd) both run in DataHub; senses fuses them: RRF, coverage rerank, per-document cap
• references come from the content plane, under character budgets
• contracts/{id}/versions — renewal lineage
• graph — a capped BFS (depth ≤ 3, 100 nodes, 500 edges) carrying corpus evidence at every hop
• ranks and resolves only — it holds no rows

div.div:
• controllers — documents · jobs · search · graph · objects (+ heads)
• coarse endpoints, because the old Python code held a transaction: ingest-submit · persist · purge · jobs/{id}/fail
• tables — documents · document_nodes (halfvec 2000) · headers · contracts · entities + aliases (trigram) · relations (evidenced) · jobs
• search returns raw-score candidates; fusion deliberately stays in senses
• objects — PUT/GET/HEAD/DELETE over bytes, manifest, header, relations, page text and images
